findings.title: Adequate handwashing sinks properly supplied and accessible.
findings.comment: There weren’t any paper towels available at the hand-sink in the employee bathroom. Discussed with the PIC and paper towels were provided to correct the violation. Ensure that paper towels are always available at all hand-sinks to be sure that hands are getting properly dried after completing the handwashing process.
findings.citation_text: 6-301.12 Hand Drying Provision. Each HANDWASHING SINK or group of adjacent HANDWASHING SINKS shall be provided with: (A) Individual, disposable towels; (B) A continuous towel system that supplies the user with a clean towel; or (C) A heated-air hand drying device; or (D) A hand drying device that employs an air-knife system that delivers high velocity, pressurized air at ambient temperatures.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
The facility has one CFPM, however, the other employee was not food handler certified. PIC noted that the other employee will be registering to take the food manager’s course soon. Ensure that all employees that handle food is food handler certified if not a CFPM. 

410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C) Facility is not in compliance with the food handler law. All food handlers, other than someone who has the food service sanitation manager certificate, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code. Food handlers working at a temporary food establishment are exempt from this requirement.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment:
410 ILCS 625 and IAC Section 750.3430 (C)  REPEAT: One of the owners had a food manager certification that expired during the pandemic. At minimum a food handler certification is required. Ensure completion of the online food handler certification or manager certification by the next routine inspection. All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.
You may complete the food handler card online at your home. There is no proctored test, only quizzlets along the way. Complete the one hour food handler card training.

findings.title: Food separated and protected
findings.citation_text:
3-302.11 Bags containing loaves of bread were stored on top of raw beef in the bottom of a reach-in cooler. Foods were rearranged to allow for proper storage with bread away from raw meat.
Food shall be protected from cross contamination during storage, preparation, holding, and display by separating raw animal foods from ready to eat foods.

findings.title: Thermometers provided & accurate
findings.citation_text:
4-203.11 Two metal stem food thermometers were available for use, with one reading around 80F and the other reading around 70F at ambient temperature. Based on information provided, thermometers were last calibrated approximately a year ago. Owner expressed knowledge on the calibration process for ice point method and verifying 32F in ice water. Thermometers were set aside to be cleaned and calibrated to ensure accuracy.
Food temperature measuring devices that are scaled only in Fahrenheit shall be accurate to ±2F in the intended range of use.

findings.title: All food employees have food handler training
findings.comment: 410 ILCS 625  Sec. 3.06 One of the owners had a food manager certification that expired during the pandemic. At minimum a food handler certification is required. Ensure completion of the online food handler certification or manager certification by the next routine inspection. All food handlers, other than someone who has a food manager certification, shall receive or obtain training in basic food handling principles as outlined in Subpart M of the Illinois Food Code.

findings.title: Hands clean and properly washed
findings.comment:
2-301.12: Observed employees wash their hands and not using a barrier when turning off the faucet. Ensure a barrier is used when turning off the faucet after washing hands. Education was provided to correct the violation. 
(A) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall clean their hands and exposed portions of arms for at least 20 seconds. (B) FOOD EMPLOYEES shall use proper procedure (C) To prevent recontamination, FOOD EMPLOYEES may use barrier to operate faucet handles. (D) Automatic handwashing facility may be used if APPROVED.

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, & used; test strips
findings.comment:
4-303.11: Observed no sani bucket being used at the start of the inspection. Ensure a sani bucket is made and available during all hours of food prep and operation. A sani bucket was made during the inspection to correct the violation. 
(A) Cleaning agents used to clean EQUIPMENT shall be provided and available during all hours of operation. (B) Chemical SANITIZERS shall be provided and available during all hours of operation.

findings.title: Utensils, equipment & linens: properly stored, dried, & handled
findings.comment: 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D)  (C) Observed clean spatulas stored wedged behind a hanging rack, which is unable to be cleaned. Spatulas moved to a magnetic strip. Equipment, Utensils, Linens and Single-Use Articles shall be stored: 1) in a clean and dry location; 2) away or protected from contamination; 3) at least six inches above the floor; 4) covered or inverted. Reference 4-903.11(A), (B) and (D).

findings.title: Proper cold holding temperatures
findings.comment: Observed sauce in the reach in cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 53 F. Sauce in the adjacent reach in cooler that was just delivered and put into service yesterday was probed at 47 and 55 F. It appears as though storing dough on the top shelves of the reach in cooler is impeding the cool air from circulating through the unit. All TCS foods out of temperature were discarded at the time of the inspection. Do not use coolers until certain they maintain foods at a temperature of 41 F or less.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B)  (P)  Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food is not maintained at 41°F, or less. Reviewed cold holding requirements and discussed HACCP concept with employee and person in charge. Inadequately held food was discarded. Reference 3-501.16(A)(2) and (B).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.comment: Observed cooked meatballs and cooked sausage in the back reach in cooler to be date marked 8-28 and 9-28 respectively. There were a few items dated 8-10 also. It was reported that those items are re-dated with a thaw date when pulled from the freezer, but one had exceeded the 7 days limit and one had not been re-dated when pulled to thaw. It appears the items dated 8-10 were meant to be dated 10-8. Items were discarded or redated as needed.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food and non-food contact surfaces cleanable, properly designed, constructed, and used
findings.comment: Observed several spatulas hanging above food prep areas that have significant chips in the food contact surfaces. Replace spatulas as needed so they are smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 4-202.11  (Pf) Food-Contact surface is no longer smooth and easily cleanable. A food-contact surface that is not smooth and easily cleanable can harbor bacteria that con be transfer to food. Replace with a National Sanitation Foundation/ANSI approved surface. Reference 4-202.11.

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition
findings.citation_text: 3-501.17  (Pf) Date of 3/23 marked on pizza sauce exceeds the time limit. Food prepared and held in a food establishment for more than 24 hours must be clearly marked to indicate the date or day by which the food must be consumed on the premises, sold, or discarded when held at a temperature of 41°F or less for a maximum of 7 days. Discussed applicable sections of 3-501.17 and reviewed HACCP concepts with person in charge. Food was discarded. Reference 3-501.17.

findings.title: Food properly labeled; original container
findings.citation_text: 3-302.12  (C) Observed food storage containers of cornmeal to not be labeled. Identify food storage containers with common name of the food. Reference 3-302.12.

findings.title: Adequate ventilation and lighting; designated areas used
findings.citation_text: 6-403.11  (C) Observed employee personal drink in cooler with food for guests.  Areas designated for employees to eat, drink, and use tobacco shall be located so that food, equipment, linens, and single-service and single-use articles are protected from contamination.

findings.title: Allergen training as required
findings.comment: PA-100-0367 - All certified food managers working in a restaurant must complete additional allergen training using an approved allergen awareness training program.

findings.title: Sanitizing concentration
findings.comment:
Observed no sanitizer solution available during food prep.  Bucket of sanitizer solution was made and tested at 200 ppm Quat.

750-800b To prevent cross-contamination, kitchenware and food-contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed and sanitized after each use and following any interruption of operations during which time contamination may have occurred.

findings.title: Hands washed, good hygienic practices (observed).
findings.comment:
750-510d To avoid re-contaminating their hands, food employees shall use disposable paper towels or similar clean barriers when touching surfaces such as manually operated faucet handles on a hand-washing sink or the handle of a restroom door.

Observed multiple employees use their bare hands to turn of the faucet with out a barrier. Discussed the proper procedure for hand washing with the PIC and suggested retraining to ensure safe practices.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed the handle to a fork on the pizza prep area to have black electrical tape on the handle and a knob on the dough roller to have duct tape and cloth on the knob. These are not smooth and easily cleanable surfaces; therefore, tape and cloth should be removed.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Thermometers, gauges, test kits provided
findings.comment:
Facility is not able to locate their quaternary ammonium test strips. Make sure to have test strips available for testing sanitizer concentration.
750-830g A test kit shall be provided and used for checking the concentration of chemical sanitizer that measures the concentration of solution in parts per million.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a personal beverage stored above cheese for the pizzas in one of the front reach in coolers. Beverage was moved during the inspection. Store all personal beverages as you store personal foods--below or away from food for the public to protect from the potential for contamination.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Plumbing installed and maintained
findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink in the kitchen to be slow draining and to fill with water while washing hands. This can either cause people to not wash their hands for a full 15-20 seconds or it may cause splash of the wastewater onto clean hands, thus re-contaminating hands. Repair plumbing so sink drains appropriately.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Original container, properly labeled, consumer advisory
findings.comment:
Observed pre-packaged brownies on the front counter to not be labeled with the ingredients. Baked goods that are packaged in advance of retail sale must have ingredients listed on the label or available.
750-110g Every food pre-packaged in advance of retail sale must bear the following information in English on its label: common name; name, address, zip code of the manufacturer, processor, packer, preparer, or distributor; net contents of package; a list of ingredients by their common or usual name; and a list of any artificial color, flavor, or preservative used.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
Observed pre-portioned lasagna in the reach in freezer to be date marked 12/13 meaning that today is Day 8. It was reported that these items were previously frozen and had been pulled to thaw on Saturday. Benefit of the doubt was given and these were re-dated to reflect Saturday's date. 2) Observed house made Ranch and Italian dressings in the cooler in the back to be date marked 12/7. It was discussed that these must be treated as potentially hazardous items and be held no longer than 7 days maximum. Dressings were discarded during the inspection. 
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous ready to eat food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the date or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
Observed personal chicken and noodles stored above cheese for pizzas in the reach in cooler in the front. It was discussed that personal foods must be labeled as such and be stored below any foods for the public. Chicken and noodles were moved during the inspection.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed single service styrofoam trays stored food contact surface up on top of the cooler in the back. Store single service items inverted to protect from  contamination. Trays were inverted during the inspection to correct the violation.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be handled and dispensed in a manner which prevents contamination of surfaces which may come in contact with food or with the mouth of the user.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed sauce in the True reach in cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 49F and milk in this cooler to be probed at an internal temperature of 52F. These items were discarded during inspection. Dough is stored on the top shelf in the reach in coolers and it was discussed that the dough may be impeding air flow in the unit. The sauce on the shelf directly below the dough was probed at 45F (however this was date marked 8/31 and was discarded) and the items probed above were on the very bottom shelf of the unit. Cooler thermostat was turned down during inspection. Monitor temperatures throughout the unit and keep a temperature log of different items internal temperatures.
750-120(a) Potentially hazardous foods, shall be maintained at a proper product temperature at all times during storage (41°F or below, or 135°F or above)

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a pie sitting on top of the dough in the True reach in cooler and the third shelf down in this cooler to be all personal foods (the bottom shelf has lettuce and sauces for the public). Personal foods should be stored in a manner where they are below and away from food for the public. It was discussed that personal foods should be stored on the bottom shelf in the cooler and drinks should have proper lids and straws. Items on the bottom shelf of this cooler were discarded as above.
750-160  Food shall be protected at all times from cross-contamination.

findings.title: In-use food dispensing utensils properly stored.
findings.comment:
Observed the scoop handle in the salt to be stored in contact with the salt. All scoops should be stored with the scoop handle extended up and out of the food.
750-280 Food dispensing utensils shall be stored in the food with the handle extending out of the food; or stored clean and dry; or stored in running potable water dipper wells.

findings.title: Non-food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed masking tape on the corner of the lid on the left on the prep cooler. Remove masking tape and repair lid with something that is smooth, easily cleanable and non-absorbent.
750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces of equipment and utensils clean
findings.comment:
1) Observed the plastic ice flap inside the ice machine to have pink slime on it. 2) Observed the can opener blade to be soiled with debris. Wash, rinse and sanitize the ice flap and can opener blade.
750-800(b) To prevent cross contamination, kitchenware and food contact surfaces of equipment shall be washed, rinsed, and sanitized after each use.

findings.title: Single service items properly stored, handled, dispensed
findings.comment:
Observed a package of pizza boxes to be sitting on the floor to the left of the True reach in cooler. Store all single service items 6" off the floor.
750-880 Single-service articles shall be stored at least six inches above the floor in closed cartons or containers which protect them from contamination and shall not be placed under exposed sewer lines or  water lines, except for automatic fire protection sprinkler heads may be required by law.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed a container of sauce dated 4/5, approximately a dozen portions of lasagna dated with various dates from January and February to 3/8, 3/10 and 3/23, and Italian beef dated 4/7 in the upright cooler. These items were discarded during inspection to correct the violation. Date mark all potentially hazardous foods and hold no longer than 7 days maximum. If these products have previously been frozen, they MUST be re-dated with the date they are pulled from the freezer and held at refrigerated temperatures no longer than 7 days total.
750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.title: Potential for cross-contamination; storage practices; damaged food segregated
findings.comment:
CORRECTED> Observed shell eggs (that were for personal use) and personal foods that were stored above the parmesan and pepper shakers as well as sauces in the upright cooler. Personal foods including shell eggs were moved to the bottom shelf during inspection to correct the violation.
750-130(d) All food shall be stored properly in order to prevent cross-contamination.  Store ready to eat foods above or a way from raw foods.

findings.title: Food contact surfaces designed, constructed, maintained, installed, located.
findings.comment:
Observed a couple spatulas hanging on the wall rack that had chipped food contact surfaces. Replace any utensils that become chipped or broken.
750-650a Food contact surfaces shall be smooth, non absorbent, easily cleanable, and free of breaks, open seams, cracks, chips, pits, and free of difficult-to-clean internal corners and crevices.

750-690 Non-food contact surfaces shall be designed and fabricated to be smooth, washable, free from unnecessary ledges, projections, or crevices and readily accessible for cleaning, and shall be of such material and in such repair as to be easily maintained in a clean and sanitary condition.

findings.comment:
Observed the hand sink to be slow draining. Repair plumbing so that sink drains appropriately and water does not pool and have the potential to splash and re-contaminate clean hands.
750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

findings.title: Cold food at proper temperatures during storage, display, service, transport, and cold holding
findings.comment:

750-151(a) Refrigerated potentially hazardous food held at the establishment more than 24 hours shall be clearly marked with the ate or day by which the food shall be consumed, sold, or discarded. Maximum holding time at 41°F is 7 days. Properly date mark food and do not hold longer than 7 days.

findings.comment:

750-1060 All plumbing shall be sized, installed, and maintained in accordance with applicable provisions of the Illinois State Plumbing Code. Repair fixtures in accordance with the Illinois Plumbing Code.

750-1200 The junctures between walls and floors shall be coved and sealed, or shall not present an opening of more that 1/32 of an inch.

750-160 Ready to eat foods shall be handled in a manner to minimize direct hand contact.

750-1210 All walls and ceilings must be in good repair and constructed to facilitate easy cleaning in order to reduce the potential for cross contamination and infestation by insects and rodents.  Provide properly constructed and clean walls and ceilings.
